visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young girl with dark hair, bangs, and two small braids on the sides is the focal point, wearing a green t-shirt with a grey shoebill bird graphic. She is seated at a light-colored table in a brightly lit indoor environment with a window visible in the background, showing soft green foliage outside. An adult female wearing a black shirt and a dark mask stands behind the girl, her hand resting on the girl's head. (2) The girl engages in various micro-actions: she leans her head to the side, smiles with her mouth slightly open, and then rests her head on her folded arms on the table. The camera remains at an eye-level, medium close-up shot, capturing her shifting facial expressions from curiosity to playful joy. (3) The scene continues with the girl covering her mouth with her hand, then yawning widely while stretching her arms upward, exposing her teeth and tongue. The lighting is consistent and warm. (4) The final phase transitions to a graphic-based animation on a solid pink background, featuring a stylized cartoon illustration of the girl sitting cross-legged, with the channel title displayed below in white uppercase text.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) Upbeat, high-tempo synthesizer BGM with a strong electronic beat starts immediately. A female adult voice speaks in a friendly, gentle tone. A bright 'ding' sound effect triggers as a subtitle appears. (2) A sharp 'pop' sound effect occurs as the mother mimes a poking action. The child's high-pitched, soft voice is heard responding with babbling. (3) The mother continues the conversation with a slightly rising intonation, asking questions. A whimsical 'cartoon whistle' SFX plays during a transition. (4) The child makes rhythmic 'po po' sounds with her lips, creating a percussive vocal texture. The mother laughs softly in the background. (5) A series of 'bubble' SFX play in quick succession, synchronized with the child's mouth movements. (6) The BGM continues at a steady pace as the child lets out a loud, high-arousal shout followed by more babbling and laughter, maintaining a cheerful atmosphere. (7) Final hard cut to the outro music, which retains the upbeat synth style but feels more like a concluding jingle, accompanied by the child's last spoken phrase.
